To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the corrosion inhibition of high speed steel by HPMC derivatives is influenced by film thickness and surface hydrophobicity, with HPMCP showing the best performance.
HPMC and HPMCAS films are effective in inhibiting the corrosion of high speed steel, while the anti-corrosion effect of the HPMC film was better than HPMCAS film.
the HPMC derivatives, HPMCP, and HPMCAS, are promising corrosion inhibitors of high-speed steel.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the use of HPMC derivatives for the corrosion protection of high speed steel.
the use of biodegradable polymers as corrosion inhibitors of high-speed steel.
the development of a novel corrosion inhibitor based on biopolymers.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
biopolymer HPMC and HPMC phthalate are promising green inhibitors for corrosion protection of high speed steel.
the corrosion inhibition performance is dependent on the chemical composition of the biopolymer derivative, the film thickness, the pH, and the immersion time.
HPMC derivatives are good corrosion inhibitors for high speed steel in 1 M H2SO4.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the biopolymers can be used as corrosion inhibitors for high speed steel, which is a promising material in the field of mechanical engineering and manufacturing.
the corrosion resistance of the high-speed steel coated with HPMCP is superior to the HPMCAS coating.
the HPMCP film is the most suitable candidate as a corrosion inhibitor for high speed steel in 1 M HCl.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the corrosion inhibition of high speed steel by HPMC derivatives can be improved with the increase in the film thickness and by the use of hydrophobic HPMCP.
the HPMC derivative film has a promising anti-corrosive performance on high speed steel surfaces.
HPMC derivatives can be used as a green corrosion inhibitor of high speed steel.
